Hi, I think that's a pretty good one, I just think it would be more interesting to add some cases with double digits like 23x Pork Sinigang to make it a bit more challenging

import re

items = input()
prices = list(map(int,input().split()))
tot=0

if items!= "None":
    for i, item in enumerate(items.split(", ")):
        tot += prices[i] * int(item.split("x")[0])

    #Clean the 1x, 2x...
    items = re.sub("[0-9]+x +","", items)

print(f"Order List: {items}")
print(f"Total Price: {tot} PHP")
Hello! If you’re interested in my solution, you can view it in my very first comment in this section. Happy learning! 💜

This is a solution I made with Python:
items = input()
prices = [int(price) for price in input().split()]
print("Order List:", items)
print("Total Price:", sum(prices), "PHP"

The solution consists of printing the first input prefixed with "Order List: " and then printing the sum of all numbers in the second input prefixed with "Total Price: " and suffixed with " PHP".

So the most challenging part of this contribution is to sum a list of numbers separated by space. In my opinion, this feels too easy and too simplistic for a Clash of Code. Do you think it's possible to add a little more complexity to your contribution?

My suggestion to make your contribution a bit more challenging and maintain the beginner-friendly attribute is to add a multiplier before each item.
For example:

**Input:**
1x Pork, 2x Chicken, 3x Tapsilog
140 130 110

**Output:**
Items: Pork, Chicken, Tapsilog
Total Price: 760 PHP

This adds two aspects:
- String manipulation: The player now needs to extract the multiplier of each order from input 1 and produce a new string without them.
- Multiplication: Instead of just summing up the values, the player also needs to multiply the price of each item by it's quantity.

This is just a suggestion. Feel free to modify it however you want.

Oh, I see! Basically, you want to multiply each price based on the quantity of items, right? That makes sense — just like how ordering works in actual practice! Thank you so much for helping me refine this work. I will gladly add it to my list. 💜

Hello @5DN1L! If you wouldn’t mind, may I ask a question? How will I know if my contribution has already been added to the website? They emailed me a long time ago about my first work, but after that I don’t know what happened — it just said it was accepted. Also, where can I see the solutions from other players when they try my puzzle? Thanks in advance! 🫠

I've never enabled the email notifications for when one of my contributions is accepted or rejected, so I'm not sure whether the email you received means your contribution has been fully approved or not. However, if you're referring to "Budget Tracker", then yes, it's been approved and can now appear in a clash of code.

In general, you can check whether your contribution has been approved, rejected or is still pending, by going to the MY CONTRIBUTIONS tab on the Contributions page (or using this link: https://www.codingame.com/contribute/my-contributions ). The box to the left of each contribution shows its current status. For example, you should see an ACCEPTED label next to your contribution "Budget Tracker".

As for viewing other players' solutions to your clash of code contributions, unfortunately that's not possible in general. The only exception is if you happen to play a clash of code where your contribution is selected and the other players choose to share their solutions with you.
